books.title: Geometric measure theory and variational problems: a first reading
books.author: Stack Project of Geometric Measure Theory and Variational Problems contributors
books.description: Original exposition connecting classical GMT, BV compactness, coarea, level-set calculus and perimeter minimization, current operations, Plateau existence, calibrated currents and singular complex curves, subcalibrations and minimizing Simons cones, smooth-support varifold constancy, exact stationary and bounded-curvature monotonicity, tangent-cone homogeneity, spine splitting, support convergence, qualitative stratification, and balanced junctions, minimal surfaces, positive Jacobi limits, ordered sheets, removable puncture stability, index localization and weak-convergence arguments, truncated power tests and Moser iteration, elliptic and Allard regularity, scalar curvature and stability, Bernstein and smooth-link cone theorems, min-max theory, compact critical sets, continuous descending fields and pull-tight deformations, stationary critical limits, concentration control, cohomological parameter arguments, metric comparison and uniform Weyl asymptotics for the volume spectrum, CMC variations and stability, Minkowski identities, constrained Jacobi fields and spectral tests, Euclidean and spherical CMC rigidity, and Allen-Cahn transition profiles, BV phase compactness, perimeter lower bounds, equipartition, recovery layers, variational limits, gradient bounds and energy monotonicity, stability, and monotone-solution rigidity. Mean curvature flow includes evolution, comparison, Gaussian monotonicity, entropy, rescaling, Brakke flow, weighted shrinker identities, Gaussian variations, symmetry modes, center/scale stability, Gaussian tails and convergence, entropy maximizers, translation factors, and entropy-lowering perturbations. Classical obstacle theory includes variational existence, reaction measures, quadratic blow-ups, Weiss and Monneau monotonicity, and singular blow-up uniqueness. Exact source editions, hypotheses, and proof status are recorded. Graphical flow includes exact angle/curvature identities, periodic convergence, noncompact maximum principles and entire graphical self-shrinker rigidity. Spherical harmonic and Sobolev expansions supply local proofs of higher gaps, mode projections and a weak inverse. Local graphical estimates include compact cutoffs, automatic curvature, rough-data comparison, height-gradient bounds and cone expanders. Arbitrary-growth entire-graph existence remains external. Current slicing includes local geometric and normal-current proofs, tangential mollification, common exceptional sets, one-sided flat continuity and explicit jump/cancellation examples. Reduced-boundary analysis includes full half-space blow-up, exact perimeter densities, countable graph covering, measure identification and general Radon differentiation with precise remaining inputs. Rectifiable tangent characterization, weighted and varifold blow-ups, intrinsic chart differentials and representative-sensitive examples are proved with explicit Whitney and Euclidean integration inputs. Rectifiable area/coarea, almost-everywhere fiber geometry, rectifiable/pure decomposition and level selection are developed with explicit Euclidean integration inputs.
